disease_label_per_paper: Rheumatoid arthritis flare presenting as prosthetic joint infection mimic
presentation_summary: 74-year-old woman with rheumatoid arthritis, atrial fibrillation, hypertension, osteoarthritis, and bilateral total knee arthroplasties presented with recurrent prosthetic-knee pain after stopping hydroxychloroquine while continuing sulfasalazine.

In May 2021 she had bilateral knee pain for several months, ESR 34 mm/h, CRP 0.78 mg/L, clear viscous synovial fluid, synovial WBC >3000 cells/uL and >65% neutrophils bilaterally, negative leukocyte esterase, negative cultures, and negative crystals.

Hydroxychloroquine was restarted and pain improved 70%. In June 2023 she developed painful left knee with ESR 57 mm/h, CRP 1.93 mg/L, synovial WBC 18,000 cells/uL with 83% neutrophils, positive alpha-defensin, negative synovial PCR, and negative cultures.

A few weeks later, repeat aspiration for NGS showed no detectable pathogenic DNA with synovial CRP 14.93 mg/L and synovial WBC 1,967 cells/uL; pain improved markedly after a 12-day oral steroid course.
Negative cultures, alpha-defensin, PCR/NGS, and improvement after RA-directed treatment are preserved as confirmatory/differential context outside ranking.
